  - Edit: ADDED new §3.1H 'ORDER BY determinism in Trino' with LEADING CANONICAL H3, inserted between L552 (§3.1G cross-refs line) and L554 (`---` separator). Contents:

Verified date 2026-06-07.
    * One-fact summary: TOP-LEVEL honored with or without LIMIT (LIMIT just enables TopN); NESTED/REDUNDANT (subquery/CTE/view/INSERT-SELECT) may be dropped; verbatim Trino docs quote.
    * Tie semantics: ORDER BY x non-deterministic among duplicate x values; add unique tiebreaker like ORDER BY x, id.
    * Worked contrast — three shapes: (1) TOP-LEVEL ORDER BY ts DESC honored, (2) NESTED (SELECT * FROM (SELECT ... ORDER BY ts DESC) t) may be dropped + the corrected outer-ORDER-BY form, (3) TIES with unique tiebreaker `ORDER BY ts DESC, event_id`.
    * 4-row DO-NOT-WRITE: (1) 'Trino strips top-level ORDER BY without LIMIT' FALSE, (2) 'LIMIT makes ORDER BY execute' FALSE (LIMIT only enables TopN), (3) 'ORDER BY in CTE/view/subquery/INSERT-SELECT guarantees ordered output downstream' FALSE, (4) 'ORDER BY ts DESC is deterministic when multiple rows share ts' FALSE among ties.
    * Decision rule for 'why does my row order vary': inner-ORDER-BY-only → move to outermost; non-unique column → add tiebreaker; unique column → look at EXPLAIN, you have a different SQL shape than you think.
    * Cross-refs: r07 §5 ROWS-vs-RANGE peer semantics, r22 §3.3A/§13.5 TopN-pushdown EXPLAIN signatures, r27 NULLS-default semantics.
